project.name: Codex of War
project.tagline: Build what the camera can judge.

activeBuild.brief: Replace the rejected procedural costume pipeline with a cohesive, professionally authored, lawfully sourced warrior character or costume. Source triage must prove a visible macro-quality upgrade before any derivative build begins; no account gate, asset name, or technical metric can substitute for the pixels.
facts: P00 is accepted as infrastructure; its blind visual baseline remains an explicit 28.33–76.67 loss.

Round 001 is mechanically reproducible: two independent critic reruns matched all six filed image hashes, P10 validation passed, focused EditMode passed 8/8, the full suite passed 14/14, and the P00 aggregate stayed byte-identical.
The randomized blind judge scored our round-001 frame 9/60 and Reference 09 49/60; the independent critic scored ours 10/60 and the reference 51/60.
Round 002 passed its mechanical export gates but failed visual preflight at 5/13. The decisive frame exposed torn and detached combat hands, so it never entered Unity.
A fresh-context critic scored round 003 at 6/13 with only 4/8 mandatory checks. The source package is a visual NO-GO and Unity was never launched.

Round 003 passed anatomy, face, feet, joint continuity, neutral coverage, and diagnostic coverage; it failed hands and grip, costume, weapon contact, materials, LOD0 budget, combat pose, and authored identity.

Two isolated Blender reruns matched semantic structure, topology, materials, and weights, but exact artifact determinism failed at 0/16 hashes for repository-to-run and 0/16 between runs. The round-003 audit also omitted its Combat FBX because its record key collided with the combat PNG.
A separate 80-deform-bone export prototype proved structural rig feasibility, but shoulder, elbow, wrist, thumb, finger, and facial-deformation hard gates remain unresolved; it is not combat-ready.

Round 004 mechanically delivered a lawful static Rain-derived source, five FBXs, nine diagnostics, and an 88,036-triangle LOD0, but a fresh critic rejected it at 7/13 with only 4/8 mandatory checks. Unity was never launched.

Round 004 passed anatomy, face, feet, joint continuity, LOD0, neutral coverage, and diagnostic coverage. It failed the second complete hand enclosure, premium costume construction, weapon function, material separation, combat intent, and unmistakable close-range AAA identity.
The single biggest gap is exact: the costume still reads as a toy-like procedural slab-and-tube assembly rather than believable, layered, worn, functional AAA warrior gear.

Two isolated Round 004 reruns matched all 26 frozen input hashes and canonical geometry, topology, UVs, materials, assignments, transforms, bounds, and near-pixel imagery. Exact output determinism still failed: only the 22 copied textures matched among 39 physical outputs.
All five Round 004 FBXs contain one broken absolute texture reference and leak the source path. The supplied validator missed this because it checks image resolution only in the authored blend.
Round 005 is a pipeline pivot, not another procedural armor polish pass. Round 001 remains the latest filed in-engine evidence until a source round clears every mandatory preflight gate.

rounds.label: Round 001
rounds.builderBrief: Wire the deterministic evidence path end to end and produce the first canonical S01 bundle.
rounds.evidence: Two independent Unity reruns matched screenshot and render-settings hashes; validator, 6/6 EditMode tests, and 4/4 dashboard tests passed. The blind visual baseline still lost 28.33–76.67.

critic.primaryGap: The current Unity frame remains a raw blockout: untextured primitive geometry and a mannequin-like hero prevent the focal character and world from reading as production-quality rendered content.

rounds.label: P10 · Round 001
rounds.builderBrief: Replace only the central hero proxy with one authored hero mesh and coherent material set while freezing the S01 seed, camera, arena, and render settings.
rounds.evidence: S01 and the four-view turntable are filed. Two fresh critic reruns matched all six image hashes; P10 validation passed, focused EditMode passed 8/8, full tests passed 14/14, and the P00 aggregate stayed byte-identical. Static lookdev only: no rig, S02, or S06.

critic.status: Rejected · fresh blind judge and critic agree
critic.primaryGap: Replace the disconnected sphere, cylinder, and cuboid plastic-mannequin hero with one continuous, anatomically credible authored shell whose face, hands, feet, joints, layered costume, weapon, and distinct skin, hair, cloth, and metal responses survive the locked S01 and four-view cameras without clipped highlights.

rounds.label: P10 · Round 002
rounds.builderBrief: Replace only the rejected plastic-mannequin hero with one continuous anatomically credible authored shell, while every locked camera, arena, seed, and render contract stays frozen.
rounds.evidence: Mechanical export passed at 65 deform bones, at most four weights, exactly two render meshes, seven material families, and 69,088 / 38,000 / 16,000 LOD triangles. Visual preflight rejected the source before Unity: the final combat proof tears and detaches both hands and does not show a physically readable grip.

critic.status: Rejected before Unity · visual gate failed closed
critic.preference: Do not advance round 002 to an in-engine blind test
critic.primaryGap: The visible combat hands tear, detach, and diverge from the rendered grip, so the weapon hold is not physically readable even though the skeletal distance proxy passes.

rounds.label: P10 · Round 003
rounds.builderBrief: Use Blender Studio Rain v3 as the high-fidelity visual foundation, apply an anime-warrior look and conforming armor/weapon pass, and prototype a truthful gameplay rig without degrading the visible source.
rounds.evidence: The CC-BY-4.0 source, generator, authored blend, exports, nine 1600px diagnostics, and independent review are filed. The critic scored 6/13 and only 4/8 mandatory checks. Two isolated Blender reruns matched semantic structure but matched 0/16 exact hashes in both comparisons. Unity was never launched.

critic.status: Rejected before Unity · fresh visual gate failed closed
critic.preference: Do not advance round 003 to Unity
critic.primaryGap: The asset has not undergone a true premium character-design transformation: it still reads as Blender Studio Rain in a civilian tank, scarf, jeans, and sneakers with thin mask-cut cyan shells, rather than an unmistakable authored anime warrior.

rounds.label: P10 · Round 004
rounds.builderBrief: Replace the rejected civilian silhouette with a cohesive head-to-toe warrior costume and material identity while preserving Rain's credible anatomy, face, hands, feet, and joint continuity.
rounds.evidence: The lawful static source, generator, validator, authored blend, five FBXs, nine 1600px diagnostics, clean-import report, and fresh independent review are filed. Mechanical import checks pass, but the visual source gate scored only 7/13 and 4/8 mandatory. Two isolated reruns matched canonical geometry and near-pixel imagery, not exact generated bytes; all five FBXs carry one broken absolute texture reference. Unity was never launched.

critic.status: Rejected before Unity · fresh visual gate failed closed
critic.preference: Do not advance round 004 to Unity
critic.primaryGap: The delivered costume's construction language is still a toy-like procedural slab-and-tube assembly rather than believable, layered, worn, functional AAA warrior gear.

rounds.label: P10 · Round 005
rounds.builderBrief: Pivot away from procedural armor construction. Start only from a lawful, cohesive, professionally authored character or costume whose fastening logic, wear, thickness, material response, and silhouette are already credible before adaptation.
rounds.evidence: Source triage found Blender Studio Einar v1: an anonymous official CC-BY payload with production layered clothing, weathered PBR surfaces, a full rig, 95 materials, and substantial 4K texture coverage. The builder verified its source receipt and is preparing a bounded Round005 visual proof. Unity remains locked.

pieces.name: Evidence spine
pieces.outcome: A deterministic review scene, fixed-seed capture command, manifest, round ledger, and live progress surface work end to end.

pieces.name: Shoulder camera
pieces.outcome: Exploration and combat framings preserve subject scale, sightline, collision, target legibility, and authored camera presets.

pieces.name: Ground locomotion
pieces.outcome: Walk, run, pivot, stop, strafe, slope handling, and camera-relative control have grounded acceleration and readable weight.

pieces.name: Hero animation foundation
pieces.outcome: Idle, locomotion, pivots, combat stance, weapon handling, additive aim, and transitions share coherent body mechanics.

pieces.name: Light combo
pieces.outcome: Buffered three-hit chain has authored startup, active, recovery, and cancel windows with one-hit-per-target resolution.

pieces.name: Heavy attack
pieces.outcome: Heavy strike communicates commitment, displacement, contact, hitstop, camera impulse, and enemy reaction.

pieces.name: Dodge and evasion
pieces.outcome: Directional dodge, invulnerability window, recovery, and camera continuity are predictable and readable.

pieces.name: Hit reaction and death
pieces.outcome: Zombies react by hit direction and severity, preserve contact, stagger, collapse, and settle without foot sliding or explosive ragdolls.

pieces.name: Zombie navigation
pieces.outcome: One zombie can acquire, approach, flank, telegraph, attack, recover, lose or reacquire, and die without navigation jitter.

pieces.name: Crowd combat director
pieces.outcome: Four-to-six zombies surround without dog-piling; attack tokens, spacing, off-screen pressure, and threat cues create readable crowd combat.

pieces.name: Hero look development
pieces.outcome: The first anime-style fighter reads as a premium authored character at gameplay and finisher distance, with coherent skin, hair, cloth, metal, and weapon materials.

pieces.name: Zombie look development
pieces.outcome: The zombie archetype and variants have layered anatomy, clothing history, damage language, silhouette variation, and material response.

pieces.name: Arena composition
pieces.outcome: A compact arena has foreground framing, combat stage, silhouette depth, traversal logic, landmarks, and no empty test-level read.

pieces.name: Lighting and atmosphere
pieces.outcome: Key, fill, rim, exposure, fog, shadows, grading, and local reactive light keep faces and contact readable while creating depth.

pieces.name: Combat VFX
pieces.outcome: Weapon trails, contact flash, sparks, debris, blood or dust, and lingering particles form a restrained macro, impact, and decay stack anchored to motion.

pieces.name: Combat audio
pieces.outcome: Foley, effort, weapon movement, contact, zombie vocals, ambience, music, ducking, and spatial mix support timing and impact.

pieces.name: HUD and threat language
pieces.outcome: Minimal health, ability, lock-on, and threat information remains legible without weakening the cinematic frame.

pieces.name: Finisher vignette
pieces.outcome: A contextual finisher has reliable setup, three-character blocking when relevant, facial and contact framing, camera choreography, and clean return to play.

pieces.name: Integrated encounter
pieces.outcome: A polished 45–90 second encounter combines the accepted systems into one authored dramatic arc.

pieces.name: Performance and delivery
pieces.outcome: The native macOS target runs reliably, captures deterministically, meets frame budgets, and ships with reproducible build instructions.

pieces.name: Fighter contract
pieces.outcome: Data-driven fighter, weapon, and ability definitions support selection without branching the shared combat core.

pieces.name: Fighter two
pieces.outcome: A distinct weapon silhouette, rhythm, traversal or combat ability, animation set, VFX identity, and finisher.

pieces.name: Fighter three
pieces.outcome: A distinct weapon silhouette, rhythm, traversal or combat ability, animation set, VFX identity, and finisher.

pieces.name: Fighter four
pieces.outcome: A distinct weapon silhouette, rhythm, traversal or combat ability, animation set, VFX identity, and finisher.

pieces.name: Roster select and persistence
pieces.outcome: Selection, preview, input, save or load, and per-fighter progression work coherently.

pieces.name: Roster encounter balance
pieces.outcome: All fighters can complete the benchmark encounter while remaining mechanically and audiovisually distinct.
